items.title: 68146_Russell Procope oral history interview
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] There was a place called Jungle Casino, with James P. Johnson. [INTERVIEWEE] I don't know that place. I don't remember that.

ctx.x: And at that point the whole band just sort of collapsed, right? Disbanded.

Well, not all at once, because they played a theater down at 14th Street, the Academy of Music. Used to be a theater down -- they still had vaudeville, sort of. And there was a fellow named Johnson who took my place, so then he -- so then that was two of the group that were out, Billy Kyle and myself. And I remember I went down and I was stationed at 110th Street at that time, so I never will

forget, it was raining real hard that day, and for the first time I put on the rainwear that the Army gives you. You know, they give you the boots and the raincoat and the -- and I put them on that day and I went to hear the band. I didn't let them know, I just sat in the audience, you know, bought a ticket and sat in the audience, and they didn't sound nothing like the Kirby band. The sound wasn't there. The precision wasn't there, you know. And I was so depressed with what being in the Army and what was…
